- Factors are the back-bone of categorical data analysis. We will utilize two packages in R, `forcats` and `haven`, combinned with `labelled`. `forcats` is specifically designed for analysing `factors` or `categerical` columns. `haven` is a specific package that we can utilize when we import data from e.g., SPSS or Stata. `labelled` is perticularly useful when we need labels, variable labels and value labels on our factor variables and the value labels. 

- We takle using Python in the main time as well, learning using `Claude`.

```{r}
libs <- c("tidyverse", "haven", "labelled", "rlang", "cli")
pacman::p_load(char = libs)
```

- We will use the `gss_cat` data connected to the `forcats` package:

```{r}
data <- list(
    gss = forcats::gss_cat
)
# list2env(data, envir = .GlobalEnv)
# write_sav(gss, "Data/R4DS/gss.sav") # we export to sav in order to use haven
```

## Importation:

One thing to start of with is that we need to be specific when we have categorical data. Check this out

```{r}
# From simple to advanced and idiotic :)

# 1. simply import! :)
gss_haven <- haven::read_sav("Data/R4DS/gss.sav")
gss_csv <- read_csv("Data/R4DS/gss.csv")

# 2. Put the data in a list and the functions in a list
data <- list(
    gss_haven = "Data/R4DS/gss.sav",
    gss_csv   = "Data/R4DS/gss.csv"
)

read <- list(
    "read_sav" = haven::read_sav,
    "read_csv" = readr::read_csv
)

# Then map :)
dat <- map2(data, read, \(data_list, reading_funcs) {
    reading_funcs(data_list)
})
list2env(dat, envir = .GlobalEnv)

# 3. More advanced list. Then pmap... :) This is stupid...
specs <- list(
    data   = c("Data/R4DS/gss.sav", "Data/R4DS/gss.csv"),
    import = c(haven::read_sav, readr::read_csv),
    name   = c("gss_haven", "gss_csv")
)
dat <- pmap(specs, \(data, import, name) import(data)) |> set_names(specs$name)
list2env(dat, envir = .GlobalEnv)
```

Okey... so after all this fancy data importation... check the data!

```{r}
gss_haven
gss_csv
```

Look at how different the frames look. The `csv` have lots of character columns, while the `haven`, or `.sav` file, has something called `haven_labelled` columns, which is both a numeric value and a value label which is attached to the specific value in the cell. 

Let's check how this works:

```{r}
sub <- gss_csv |> 
    select(marital) |> 
    mutate(marital = fct(marital)) # factor levels by how they appear in the column
levels(sub$marital)

sub <- gss_haven |> 
    select(marital) |> 
    mutate(marital = as_factor(marital)) # Underlying numeric code keept and fixed
levels(sub$marital)

sub <- gss_haven |> 
    select(marital) |> 
    mutate(marital = as_factor(marital, levels = "both")) # Keep the numeric code, fixed and visible
levels(sub$marital)

sub |> count(marital) |> 
    mutate(marital = str_remove_all(marital, "\\[[^\\]]*\\]")) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = n, y = marital)) + geom_col() + theme_classic()
```

```{r}
sub <- gss_haven |>
  select(marital) |>
  mutate(
    marital = {
      labs <- attr(marital, "labels", exact = TRUE)   # etikett -> kod
      old  <- labs[["No answer"]]
      vals <- as.numeric(marital)
      vals[vals == old] <- 999
      labs[labs == old] <- 999
      haven::labelled(vals, labels = labs, label = attr(marital, "label", exact = TRUE))
    }
  )

attr(sub$marital, "labels")

sub <- sub |> mutate(marital = as_factor(marital))
levels(sub$marital)
```
